rubrics.name: source_population_catalog_controls
rubrics.rubric: In the required final source_register.xlsx, establish the complete pre-analysis catalog population requested in the conversation and keep modeled bridge rows visibly separate from official catalog records. Grade the submitted evidence semantically; worksheet names and layout are not requirements.
disclosure: User turn 24 requests every source record before analysis.
The resumed register, raw catalog bundles, and lineage manifest expose the catalog population and row fields.
criterion: Makes exactly 1,514 official catalog trade records directly verifiable and does not count modeled bridge or summary rows as official catalog records.
Provides or makes directly countable the catalog-year controls 2015 = 263, 2016 = 251, 2017 = 500, and 2019 = 500.
Preserves row-level identifiers and the source fields needed to audit scope, including year, flow, partner dimensions, transport mode, value, inclusion status, and governing rule.

rubrics.name: source_quality_and_governance_controls
rubrics.rubric: In the required final source_register.xlsx, preserve the source-quality and current-governance decisions that control downstream work. Grade the submitted evidence semantically; worksheet names and layout are not requirements.
disclosure: User turns 24 and 35 request quality decisions, current governing versions, and result-changing supersession.
Workspace quality flags, method releases, forecast setup, calendar material, and checkpoint governance sheets disclose the decisions and parameters.
criterion: Excludes the invalid Census HTML and empty BLS series from numeric evidence while treating the Comtrade gap as a coverage control handled through the governed bridge.
Uses REV-MR-22-02 for headline total-row aggregation and REV-MR-23-03 / MODEL-BRIDGE-23-03 for the current forecast, recovery benchmark, and continuity threshold.
Carries the current 92% recovery benchmark and GBP 35,000 ERP-level threshold, and ties material decisions to concrete workspace evidence or business identifiers.

rubrics.name: entity_resolution_across_systems
rubrics.rubric: Across the required final source_register.xlsx and continuity_exposure.xlsx, resolve procurement, supplier-portal, BOM, and tariff identifiers to a stable ERP entity. Grade equivalent crosswalk and reconciliation evidence regardless of worksheet names or layout.
disclosure: User turn 35 explicitly requests resolution of trade, procurement, supplier portal, BOM, and tariff identifiers to the same entity.
The material catalog, supplier appendix, order board, receipts, and resumed Entity_Resolution sheet disclose the mappings.
criterion: Maps ERP-OC-1042 to acetonitrile, MRS-884, BOM-ACN-17, HS 292690, GBP 7.40 per kg, and its relevant purchase orders somewhere in the connected package.
Also maps ERP-OC-2055, ERP-OC-3188, and ERP-OC-7710 to their supplier portal, BOM, tariff, cost, and procurement identifiers.
Uses ERP code as the stable continuity key and treats other identifiers, including receipt order references, as mapped attributes or matching aids rather than independent entities.

rubrics.name: analysis_headline_total_and_gap_basis
rubrics.rubric: In the required final analysis_workbook.xlsx, use the governed all-world export-total basis and preserve the source distinction behind the 2019 export gap. Grade equivalent analysis evidence regardless of worksheet names or layout.
disclosure: User turns 1 and 15 diagnose the source-coverage mismatch and require the official-versus-modeled distinction.
The trade totals, governed bridge, manifest, method releases, and resumed analysis workbook disclose the basis and values.
criterion: Uses all-world headline total rows rather than stacking partner, route, or transport-mode rows.
Reports 2015 exports about USD 13,948,039,379 and 2017 exports about USD 10,576,287,128, each within 1% tolerance.
Marks the 2019 export value as macro_bridge or equivalent modeled status and uses the governed value of about USD 11,883,876,287 rather than zero-filling or substituting imports.

rubrics.name: analysis_recovery_and_forecast_from_register
rubrics.rubric: In the required final analysis_workbook.xlsx, carry the register-controlled bridge, recovery benchmark, and current forecast method into the numeric analysis without imposing worksheet, deck, or memo placement requirements.
disclosure: User turns 45, 49, and 60 require the numeric workbook to be downstream of the register and use its population, quality, and version choices.
The forecast setup, governed bridge, method releases, and resumed numeric workbook expose the recovery and forecast calculations.
criterion: Reports the 2019 bridge baseline around USD 11,883,876,287, 2020 at about 80.10% of baseline, and 2021 at about 102.45% of baseline, with 2021 clearing the 92% benchmark.
Reports 2023 forecast exports within USD 11.126-11.465 billion and 2024 forecast exports within USD 9.656-9.951 billion.
Identifies the forecast as the current REV-MR-23-03 / MODEL-BRIDGE-23-03 bridged-history method and keeps modeled values distinct from official observations.

rubrics.name: po_population_and_reconciliation
rubrics.rubric: Across the required final source_register.xlsx and continuity_exposure.xlsx, reconcile the complete purchase-order population using the workspace receipt and normalization decisions. Grade equivalent reconciliation evidence regardless of worksheet names or layout.
disclosure: The final user turn requests a reconciled continuity-exposure workbook on the register-controlled basis.
The order board, receipt extract, receiving runbook, receipt email, logs, and checkpoint procurement sheets disclose the population and dirty-record handling.
criterion: Shows open quantities of 21,850 kg, 0 kg, 5,500 kg, 15,000 kg, and 0 kg respectively, either directly or through transparent reconciliation.

Demonstrates that partial fulfillments were reconciled and identifies at least one relevant workspace-documented matching, reversal, status, or UK-date normalization issue; evidence may be split between the controlled register and continuity workbook.

rubrics.name: calendar_and_reserve_application
rubrics.rubric: Across the required final continuity_exposure.xlsx and decision_memo.docx, apply the working-calendar exception and finance-reserve rule. The calculation and narrative evidence may be split between the files; worksheet names and layout are not requirements.
disclosure: The final user turn requests continuity exposure reconciled from the governed register basis.
The working calendar, calendar notice, reserve email, operational rules, and resumed analysis disclose the dates and reserve parameter.
criterion: Calculates PO-2022-10488 delivery as 2023-01-05 after applying the additional 2022-12-28 non-working inbound day.
Preserves the 2023-01-04 dock target and makes clear that the governed delivery is later than that target.
Applies the documented 12% finance or expedite reserve consequence to the affected exposure.

rubrics.name: tier_chain_exposure_and_transition_exception
rubrics.rubric: Across the required final continuity_exposure.xlsx, risk_map_deck.pptx, and decision_memo.docx, calculate the Atlas-to-MiraSolv exposure and apply the transition exception consistently. Grade equivalent calculation and decision evidence regardless of worksheet, slide, or section names.
disclosure: The final user turn requests a continuity-exposure package reconciled from the same governed basis.
Supply pathways, the 58% throughput log, material costs, reserve evidence, and the CR-2219 email disclose every factor and the exception treatment.
criterion: Treats Atlas Nitriles / ATN-044 at 58% throughput as a 42% loss and propagates it using REL-ACN-31 at 0.64 and REL-ACN-42 at 0.72.
Reports a combined impacted fraction of 0.193536 and impacted quantity about 4,228.76 kg for PO-2022-10488 within 1% tolerance.
Reports ERP-OC-1042 risk-adjusted exposure around GBP 35,047.98 and treats the threshold breach as a CR-2219 transition-watch item rather than a supplier-policy violation.

rubrics.name: remaining_entity_risk_classification
rubrics.rubric: In the required final continuity_exposure.xlsx and downstream package, preserve the reconciled exposure values and threshold classifications for the remaining ERP entities. Grade equivalent risk evidence regardless of worksheet names or layout.
disclosure: The final user turn requests one internally consistent continuity package.
The order, receipt, cost, threshold, and entity-resolution evidence in the workspace supports these rows.
criterion: Identifies ERP-OC-3188 / PO-2022-10502 and ERP-OC-7710 / PO-2022-10508 as the next two positive-exposure entities after ERP-OC-1042.
Reports exposures around GBP 10,065 for ERP-OC-3188 and GBP 9,300 for ERP-OC-7710, each within 1% tolerance.
Classifies both below the GBP 35,000 threshold and does not present them as supplier-policy actions.

rubrics.name: cross_artifact_internal_consistency
rubrics.rubric: Treat the five required final files source_register.xlsx, analysis_workbook.xlsx, continuity_exposure.xlsx, risk_map_deck.pptx, and decision_memo.docx as one internally consistent package. Worksheet, slide, and section names are not graded.
disclosure: User turns 45 and 49 establish register-first downstream work.
The final user turn names all five deliverables and explicitly requires one internally consistent set.
criterion: Provides all five named deliverables under /app/output.
Keeps the official-versus-modeled distinction, governing versions, forecast posture, entity identities, threshold, and exception treatment consistent across the files that discuss them.
Uses the same risk IDs or equivalent entity labels and the same exposure values and decisions in the continuity workbook, deck, and memo, without contradictory independent recomputation.
